utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-04-75-T, the Prosecutor versus Goran Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. May we have the appearances please, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. Douglas Stringer, Alex Demirdjian, Thomas Laugel, and Lucia Laporte for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Zivanovic, for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For the Defence of Goran Hadzic, Zoran Zivanovic and Christopher Gosnell. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The witness may be brought in. And just to be sure that it is on the record, we will not sit on the 27th of May. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Let's see whether we can finish your testimony in this first session. Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I certainly think we can do that Mr. President. Thank you. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 6122 back up on the screen, please, which is the document we were looking at when we finished yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Theunens, you remember that one of the first questions I asked you at the beginning of this cross-examination was whether inspection is an indication of authority. And you said, well, it depends on the context and please show me the context and the documents. And here we have a document and a context. Do you think in this context that inspecting these local TOs staffs, local communes, police stations, is that an indication of authority?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, yes, indeed. Looking at the document and paragraph 1 as to who will conduct those inspections, I agree with Mr. Gosnell's proposition.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: If we could go please to the bottom of the page 4 in the English. Item 7. Yes, there it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And what we see in item 7 is some support for your review about the advisory function. It says the town command officers be included as groups of advisors to the executive council of the municipality where the town command is, et cetera. And then if we turn the page, item 8: "This order shall be realised quickly and efficiently by strictly adhering to the deadlines as this is a precondition for the territory of the SO to be organised satisfactorily for the arrival of UN peacekeeping forces. "The civilian affairs organs, town commands, and municipal executive councils are responsible for the accurate and timely execution of this order." Now do you see here, Mr. Theunens, that what's happening is that an order is being issued by this JNA commander not only to elements of the JNA but to the municipal executive councils?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I -- I mean, the -- see the list -- list of addressees, maybe I mentioned at the beginning of the document or maybe at the end. I can only see half of a page on this screen, so ... because that could be of assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: There are no addressees indicated on the document.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, then, I mean, this would be the -- if I would agree with you, it would be the first time that I see a JNA document where a JNA officer is ordering municipal authorities. The proposition you make I would not agree with you. I would also like to emphasise it's not quote unquote my view, but it's just -- it's sufficient to read the various instructions from the SSNO and the 1st Military District from November and December 1991 in order to really establish that the JNA from the 20th of November onwards only has a supporting role in relation to civilian authority and their establishment -- and its establishment, I'm sorry. That -- yeah, that the JNA has only a supporting role in relation to civilian authority and its establishment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 6172, please. Prosecution tab 650. This is from Major-General Mico Delic commander of the 1st Mechanized Corps. It's dated either the 1st or the 3rd of April, 1992. It's addressed to the commands of the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 453rd, Mechanized Brigade and the 252nd Armoured Brigade, and the town command of Ilok and Mirkovci. "Although this command, and particularly its organ for civil affairs, pointed out a number of times and issued written orders regulating the procedure of how the unit commands and town commands are to deal with found and abandoned state and private property and facilities. There have been instances of omissions and weaknesses and for this reason we once again point out the following ..." "Commissions should be formed with the local civilian authorities to inventory and seal it; use of found appropriate and facilities is within the purview of the local civilian authorities which must regulate their distribution and the right to use by other persons with a decision, record, and other written documents in close co-operation with the town commands." "Unit and town commands and particularly the organs for civilian affairs and its officers must monitor the work of the local civilian authorities, offering advice and guidance in the matter in order to adopt the right decisions which would benefit the local inhabitants." Does that appear to you to reflect purely an advisory function?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Advisory and assisting function.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You wouldn't infer any sense of control, authority, direction in respect of those activities?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we should make a distinction. This order is sent to a number of JNA units and more specifically the organs within these JNA units that constitute town commands. In relation to them, yes, there are strict instructions. But overall, when it comes to the subject matter of dealing with abandoned property - and there the trial can see the other paragraphs of the document, for example paragraph 3 and 4 - again, it -- it is consistent with the earlier instructions and orders I have mentioned already a few times during the past days concerning the role of the JNA and its support to the local SAO SBWS civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We tender this document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit D54. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: 6165, please. Prosecution tab 645.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This is from the Command -- commander of the 252nd Armoured Brigade, a certain Jovan Vuckovic. Report on the selection and appointment of officers to command duties in police organs. Jovan Stevic, son of Aleksandar, lieutenant-colonel in the armoured mechanized unit, et cetera, has expressed a wish to be appointed Chief of Staff of the Vukovar police brigade with the establishment rank of lieutenant-colonel." He is now temporarily working in the 252nd Armoured Brigade." What is this about and what units are being referred to?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, this is what we saw in the examination; that is, in spring 1992 prior to the arrival of UN peacekeeping troops in -- in the UNPAs, so the United Nations Protected Areas as defined by the Vance Plan, the SSNO issues instructions to establish an RSK TO, i.e., to restructure existing units and so on, but to come to a more uniform and organised structure, and it includes also a support, I think even similar support, in relation to an RSK MUP, i.e., police, and for what Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem is concerned this also includes the transfer of JNA personnel to the -- to the RSK and in this case SBWS MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And what role do you say the JNA has in the appointments?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have seen documents that they appoint people but at this moment I'm not sure -- I mean, if you can show me the document again. I'm sorry to repeat this. This is all from the new -- I think this is part of the new report and there, if I had the new report in front of me, I could point you to other documents. Now I just have to look at each document separately and try to recall which document I saw in which trial which over a time-period of nine years is a bit of a challenge. But what I'm trying to say is that I have seen documents that the JNA is appointing personnel to the RSK TO. At this moment, I don't recall whether the JNA or the SSNO is also appointing personnel to the RSK MUP. In this document here, there is just an expression of interest of a JNA member to become a member of the RSK MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you remember that there's still an imminent threat of war in effect in the SFRY as of this date; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you say so, you know, I recall a decision --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I do say so and maybe I can just -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... if I can answer the question that was. Your Honours, I remember that a decision is adopted at one moment in time, I think it's later in 1992, to retract this imminent state of war. Now, none of the documents we have seen so far, none of the SSNO documents I have seen and we have discussed makes a reference to this decision or to this state of imminent threat of war, so I'm not sure to what extent it was really determining the events. We are looking at a very de facto situation where - and again, this is something I mentioned over the past days, but I think it's important to clarify it again - where existing laws are being bent and adjusted in order to implement certain measures and where bodies that are not foreseen in SFRY legislation as SAOs and their civilian authorities and their own TO legalized and -- and -- and again, so for me the determining factor is not whether or not a state of imminent threat of war was really into effect at that moment in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We may have lost the LiveNote, Mr. President. At least as it comes through the computers. If Your Honours are all right, we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm fine, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. We have it on one screen and on the other screen, that's the screen that you can mark, where you can mark the transcript. So we have no problem for the moment. If you don't, we can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I can proceed, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We would tender that document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honours. This one has already been admitted and marked as P1697. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have P1704, please, which is Prosecution tab 661.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This is -- [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This is from the civilian affairs organ of the -- well, it doesn't say which unit. But they are reporting to the command of the 1st Mechanized Corps and they're reporting on the state of the police in Mirkovci village. So again this is the same village we've been talking about. It says: "Pursuant to the work-plan of organs for civilian affairs of the 1st Mechanized Corps command an inspection and review of the state of the Mirkovci police station was carried out on 15 May [sic] 1992 ..." Then there is a discussion of the condition of the police station. And if we could go to page 2 at the bottom we see some conclusions. And the conclusion is: "In terms of personnel and expertise, the police station can carry out its functional duties following the withdrawal of the JNA from this area, but the question of supplying the peacetime force with weapons, uniforms, communications equipment, meals, and fuel needs to be resolved. The personnel allocated on a temporary basis from the Serbian MUP are expressing dissatisfaction with the whole system of organisation of the police in Krajina and have therefore filed a request for their withdrawal, which would severely undermine the police station's system of work." So am I right that and do you know from other documents that the Serbian MUP was still involved in setting up or shoring up police stations in this area around let's say into May 1992?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think we also addressed that during examination, that is, that as is indicated in the documents up -- at least up to the deployment of UN forces in the area, there was a presence of members of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia in SBWS, and from my activities outside ICTY, and more specifically when I was serving in peacekeeping operations, in -- in the Balkans, we understood - when I say "we" that was UNPROFOR - that there was still, I mean, even up to 1995, a presence of members of the MUP Serbia in SBWS including as members of the local Serb police.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I appreciate your reference to your own UNPROFOR experience, and I'd ask you to draw on that with my next question. When you read that final conclusion, would you agree that it seems that the JNA is scrutinising whether conditions are ripe for a hand-over to the UNPROFOR forces? Is that the point?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe it's -- it's a question of language. I mean, English is not my first language, but I would word it slightly different because it's not so much -- I mean, the hand-over to the UN is -- is not something to decide -- or not part of the Vance Plan, I'm sorry. The Vance Plan foresees demilitarisation, demobilization, and disbanding of local armed structures, as well as withdrawal of the JNA and the ZNG. That's one aspect of the Vance Plan. A second aspect is the deployment of a lightly armed UN force. But there is no formal hand-over foreseen in the Vance plan between the JNA and UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: The SFRY is a party to the Vance agreement and the JNA is an organ of the SFRY, so what I'm asking is do you think that what's going on here is pursuant to perceived obligations by the JNA vis-a-vis the Vance Plan?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What we can say is that the SFRY -- that excuse me. The SFRY political authorities are concerned about the situation in -- in -- in the -- in the territory covered by the RSK. And in relation then to the specific paragraph, yeah, they want to know what is the -- the state of -- of -- of functioning or the state of readiness is of the RSK police because according to the Vance Plan this is the only armed structure the Serbs are allowed to maintain in the UNPAS.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Is it the JNA's obligation as an organ of the SFRY to ensure that those conditions are fulfilled?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I'm reluctant to use the word or the expression "obligation" because I have seen orders, and as I mentioned earlier to the JNA, to provide support to assisting in -- in -- in organising the RSK TO even if it's not allowed anymore according to the Vance Plan, but I haven't seen a document or I don't recall seeing a document that the JNA is -- is obliged or is ordered by the SFRY political authorities to ensure the -- the -- the complete state of readiness or the highest state of readiness of the RSK police.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You testified at page 4309: "It was well-known that there were disputes or, in particular, among the JNA, about the nature of the conflict, whether it was an international or an internal armed conflict." Can you tell us who thought it was an international armed conflict?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not -- we would have to look at the 27th of November memorandum, that is, I think we discussed it during examination. That is this agreed between JNA or SFRY armed forces, the Croatian side, I think there were people there from the ZNG --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's bring that up for your benefit, Mr. Theunens, just before you continue with your answer. It could assist you in your answer, sir.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 00722, which is I believe Prosecution tab 211.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So there it is. I don't know if there's a particular page you'd like to look at, sir.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I don't know by heart in which page this is being discussed, but what I was trying to say that is that then there is a reply to that, and this is in the amalgamated report, where I think the member of the legal administration in the SFRY armed forces state, well, irrespective of this and this and this, i.e., the memorandum, we consider the conflict still an internal conflict. My reference to what I called dispute or -- yeah, dispute concerning the nature of the conflict, I also remember from my - and this is not from documents but from my participation in witness interviews, and these witnesses were senior JNA officers, that some of them stated, for example, that only after October 1991, i.e., when the moratorium imposed by the European community at that time on Croatia's declaration of independence of -- of 25th of June 1991, when that moratorium had expired, that then, well, okay, at that -- only at that moment the conflict transformed into an international armed conflict. You will see that in none of my reports in all those years I have dealt with the question of whether it was an international or a -- or not an international armed conflict because this is really outside my expertise. When answering the question, I only tried to provide information I had come across while working here and while reviewing documents, without issuing any -- any opinion or any analysis to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Does it follow from the fact that certain JNA officers considered this to be an international armed conflict, as you say, that they considered the SBWS region to be occupied territory?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I cannot answer that question, Your Honours, because it's -- it's too -- I mean, first of all, it's too broad, and secondly I didn't go into, I mean, when participating with these -- participating in witness interviews for senior JNA officers, I didn't go into discussion of whether it was national or international conflict because, again, it's -- for me it's a legal issue that is outside the scope of my professional activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, you've talked about the JNA's understanding of international criminal law and how that's incorporated into SFRY legislation. That appears to be within what you consider the scope of your report. You can't tell us whether under SFRY law if a conflict is considered international, that the territory occupied in the other state is considered occupied territory when the JNA is present there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I -- I think I answered the question. I can -- I can repeat what I consider most relevant elements of my answer. That is, that I haven't seen any -- except for the comment by the legal administration on this memorandum, I haven't seen any JNA documents indicating that it's -- whether it's an internal or an international conflict. I don't remember seeing in the various reports and orders at the various levels of command SFRY armed forces, the military districts, operation groups, or tactical groups any change in approach between let's say the period prior to October 1991 and after October 1991, so there's not much more -- not much -- anything else relevant I can say to this -- to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I suppose that also means that you can't tell us anything about whether or not the JNA considered itself bound by any specific or particular obligations based on that view that it was an international armed conflict and according to me that that was occupied territory?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell, I -- I mean, I don't dispute your view because I have nothing relevant to say about it for the Trial Chamber. I think there are other witnesses who are better qualified to that. I mean, your view on occupied territory, but the JNA did not consider itself bound. I mean, please have a look at the instructions by Kadijevic, Adzic, Panic, I mean, and the other generals in relation to the obligation of the JNA and its subordinate forces at all times to abide by the international laws of war. Maybe they don't specifically refer to the internationals laws of war as a concept, but we have the 1988 regulations which were valid during the conflict. We have also the various orders and instructions where they talk about the need for proper treatment of the civilian population, prisoners, prevent looting, and so on and so on. So the JNA was aware of -- of these obligations.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have P171, please, Prosecution tab 596.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sir, you've looked at this document during your direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Registrar, for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And I've noticed that you're very good on occasion at noticing translation mistakes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure what you mean by "on occasion."

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I mean, sometimes I've notice that you catch translation mistakes, and I'm going to direct your -- so what I'm saying is that I know that you have some facility in B/C/S; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, after eight years I think it's reasonable to expect that one would be able to -- to understand a little bit of or at least some -- a little bit, yeah, sorry, of military terminology.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, if we can look at the second paragraph and if you could focus your attention on the B/C/S second paragraph, can you tell us whether it says that the Serbian region of Baranja, East Slavonia, and west Srem will be represented by the prime minister?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't. I mean, I see -- I see President Zunik Vlade and ministry and so on, but, I mean, which are not so difficult to understand those expressions, but I wouldn't be able to find a verb or to -- to -- to establish from the B/C/S what their role would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could with we have the interpreters, please, read the words following on from where it says "while the Serbian region." I'm not sure if they have the document in front of them, the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you give us a more precise reference on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yes. It's the second paragraph of the document. And it's the words following from: "... while the Serbian region ..." Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The representative of the government. A representative of the government, ministers of the interior, and national defence, and the commander of the TO staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, did you hear the translation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I missed the first part because I just heard the name of individuals or functions, but not more.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: The interpreter translated it as a representative of the government.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: One letter, the letter A, is missing in the word representative, "Predstvnik," the letter A is missing. It's just a typo.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So there appears to be a typographical error but the word is nevertheless representative, aside from that typographical error.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honours. I see that there is -- I mean, whereas the English text refers to prime minister. Given -- based on the translation we hear now, it -- in fact it should be somebody else. If I understood -- yeah, I think that is the point you wish to make, but I guess -- I mean, it's easy to establish. You don't need me for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have P17 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell, is this as far as you go with this translation error or will you tender a revised translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'm not sure what the right procedure is but we would make a request to CLSS for a revised translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I think that would be appropriate, yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Apparently a request has already been made, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: P1710, please. Prosecution tab 586.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, sir, this is -- as it's coming up on the screen, it's a report by Milos Miljevic, the assistant commander for civil affairs. He's a colonel in the 1st Proletarian Mechanised Division, and he's reporting on the government session as it says in the subject line, and just to contextualise this document, sir, you might remember that this -- this follows the exchange of letters between Mr. Hadzic and Mr. Belic, Colonel Belic in Ilok. And there -- so this appears to be some kind of a follow-up. Well, it may not be. We don't know. But in any event, that's what it might be.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And if we -- sorry, sir, did you want to say something?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I mean, I think you answered the question yourself. I understand that -- I mean, there's the exchange of letters of the 23rd of December, 25th of December, and this is happening on the 31st of December. Whether there's any link between the two, I cannot establish. Certainly not when just seeing document by document on the screen. But I think you answered that yourself, that we don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I appreciate that. Thank you. Now if we could go to page 2, please. And you commented on this document during your direct examination. What we see -- the words that we see reported there as having been uttered by the person identified as the deputy prime minister, namely Bogunovic, the words that are reported as being uttered are: "We do not know what our goals are. We want the structure here to change. Some people do not understand military administration well." Now, just looking at those words before we go on to the interpretation given by the officer here, those words don't in any way condone or indicate that the policy of the government of the SBWS is ethnic cleansing, do they?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But I think the military -- I mean, the drafter of the report doesn't use the expression "ethnic cleansing." He talks about to change the structure of the population. He adds "at all costs," whereas the deputy prime minister talks about "we want the structure here to change." I can only rely on the conclusion of the drafter of the document that the deputy prime minister, when using the expression "structure," actually means the structure of the population. When I say I can only rely on the views expressed by the drafter, then I -- of the document, then I will also look at other documents, and then I see that actually this -- this conclusion by the drafter of the document is supported by the developments on the ground during that time-period.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, developments on the ground doesn't mean it's government policy, does it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we would have to look at the documents. And again, I'm sorry to repeat it, but in the -- in the report I compiled in September, I -- I put all the documents that were available to me and my conclusion was that there was a pattern whereby the government at least condones, i.e., doesn't prevent, and according to JNA officers, some members or people affiliated with the SAO SBWS government actually actively participate in changing the ethnic structure of the population during that time-period. And just to finish it, I don't think we have discussed these -- these reports, but the reports of the UN Secretary-General on the implementation of the mandate date of the UN peacekeeping forces in Croatia during 1992, I quote from a number of them, indicate or actually confirm that this harassment and other pressure on members of minorities is continuing throughout 1992 and even later.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yet none of the documents at all show that anyone in the district government is in any way active - as you just said now - none of the documents show that anyone from the district government is involved in events of ethnic cleansing or putting pressure on Croats to leave. Unless you take for -- as true the allegation that Devetak is somehow a part of the district government, which we say he certainly isn't.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, that's your view. You know, I would -- maybe the Prosecution is going to bring up these documents again, but I don't know by heart all the documents I have included in the new report so I can't answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But just coming back to the words that are reported as having been said by Bogunovic. When he says we want the structure here to change, and then that's immediately followed by a reference to some people do not understand military administration well, doesn't it seem to that you the structure that's being complained about or that needs to be changed has to do with martial law in this area, which is basically what I say we have?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, yeah, I remember you referred in the previous days that there was military rule, and I remember in the reply Colonel, I think, Begic sends to General Hadzic on the 25th December 1991, he puts military rule between quotation marks or he express some doubts about the use of the expression "military rule" in reply to the letter of Hadzic of the 23rd of December, 1991, now use martial law. I don't remember that martial law was in effect in SBWS at that moment. Again, show me a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, it's the imminent -- it's the declaration of the imminent threat of war of the 1st of October, 1991, which is still in effect into May, I say. But I really don't want to get bogged down in that detail. What I'm going to now do is just proceed to the next couple of sentences in this report because I think they're quite vital to understanding what really is being expressed here. And what it says, and I suggest that you've misread this, Mr. Theunens, just to be clear. What it says is: "These quotes illustrate that the government wants to change the structure of the population at all costs. Even by pushing them under the impact of artillery in the zone of intense combat activities, 'while we do not know what our goal is,' can mean that 'why doesn't that army free the whole of Slavonia and hand us over the authority on a plate?' "His support of immigration, even in the zone of intense combat activities did not cease even after the warning by a representative of the Division Command that we did not recommend populating refugees to the west of Tovarnik to spare them from experiencing exodus twice." Now let's just understand where Tovarnik is. Isn't it right that Tovarnik is a village that's close to the confrontation line with Croatian forces? In fact, it's the western limit, if I can just remind you, of the southern area, if you recall.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's the south western limit, and I think it's close to the highway -- I mean, where the highway cuts or crosses through Western Srem. It's on the western -- south-western limit of the -- of the confrontation line as it is in that time-period.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And if you look at the passage that I just read, you see two references to intense combat activities, and I suggest that that shows that these two concepts are linked and that what this colonel is complaining about is not that the district authorities are talking about forcing Croats out of the area. He's talking about forcing the Slavonian refugees to move into areas that the army considers unstable. Isn't that what's being talked about here in terms of changing the structure of the population?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree with you if there wasn't the word "even" in the fourth line, or -- sorry, near the fourth line of that paragraph, because for sure he is talking about immigration, i.e., the resettlement of Serbian refugees from other areas. Resettlement in Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. But I don't think it's -- it's -- he is exclusively talking about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Why does the word "even" change that? Here we have the person expressing alarm or he is disconcerted and that's why he uses the word "even" because he is suggesting that the district government is pushing people into these areas even though they're unstable. There is artillery being fired there. Isn't that why he is using the word "even"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: For me, the -- the use of the expression "even" means that there are -- the population structure is also changed in other matters -- manners, sorry, in other ways. And that -- I mean, the most serious -- or the most negative, ways, I'm sorry, of changing the population is by pushing them under the impact of artillery according to the author of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Aside from this document and the previous document, have you seen any indications that there were any contacts between the JNA and the district government of the SBWS from August 1991 until May 1992?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to answer the question, Your Honours, because I don't have the documents in front of me. I mean, all these questions you are asking are referring to documents that were made available after the expiration of the deadline for the submission of the amalgamated report. In the amalgamated report, I think there are very few documents we never -- I mean, my view is that because never obtained such documents from -- from FRY or Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sir, you said you are not a political analyst and you have said that commenting on the legal implications of the Law on All People's -- excuse me, on the legal implications of a declaration of imminent state of war are beyond your expertise, and yet you have quite comfortably, based on your review of RSK legislation, come to the conclusion - which I suggest is a quasi-legal conclusion - that Mr. Hadzic as president or as prime minister of the RSK becomes Commander-in-Chief of the RSK armed forces. How is it, considering that you don't speak B/C/S, you claim you're not an expert in legal matters, and you don't know the political background that might assist in understanding the Law on Defence that was passed, how is it that you are able to come to the conclusion that the provisions in that law mean that Mr. Hadzic is the Commander-in-Chief?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please show me the passage in my report where I use the expression "Commander-in-Chief" because I don't recall that. I usually use the expression or the language used in the documents and there it's "Supreme Commander."

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'll correct myself. You did use the words "Supreme Commander" and it was during your testimony here.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, then I would -- I think it would help to have the law in front of us, and then if it says that the president of the republic is -- commands the armed forces in those and those conditions or is the Supreme Commander, I don't think one needs to be a legal expert to understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: If you could go to page 370 of your report, sir, and while we're doing that if we could also bring up L46, please, which is somewhere on the Prosecution's list. And if we could go to page 3 of L46, which is Article 6.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, what I was trying to say is that when you look at the article, Article 6 of the 1992 RSK Law on Defence, it states: The president of the republic leads, I mean title 1, leads the armed forces in the peacetimes and in times of war. I don't think it -- it requires a legal expertise to understand what the role of the president then is in relation to the armed forces. I think it's also -- should also be clear that, for example -- I mean, in any country an officer pleads allegiance to the constitution and the laws of his war. I did the same in Belgium in 1984, if I remember well. Well, it wouldn't make much sense to plead allegiance to something that I don't understand as a military officer, so I would be confident that officers serving in the SVK or prior to that the RSK TO understood what was meant by, for example, this first sentence of Article 6 without having a degree in law or other legal expertise.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Is the prime minister in a parliamentary system with cabinet responsibility the Supreme Commander of the forces in that country?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would have to look at the specific document because each country may have its own definition and its own provisions as to who is the Supreme Commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So you allow that that might not be the case, that the person who is the prime minister is not necessarily the Supreme Commander of the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell, I think this is a fair question to the witness, to be urged to answer questions about other systems he didn't -- he didn't examine?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I'm -- I'm attempting to explore the concept as to whether the person who is identified as the senior political figure, in quotation marks, must of necessity be the Supreme Commander, and that was a concept that was relied on by Mr. Theunens in his direct testimony when he said that Mr. Hadzic must be the Supreme Commander because he was the leading political figure. So it's the concept that I'm attempting to explore. I don't -- I don't know what was the basis, Mr. President, for him saying that at this stage.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mean, please show me the -- please show me the transcript, then, because also I -- I think I don't use expressions like "leading political figure" because I -- I -- what I do when review the documents is I try as much as possible to use the language or to refer to the language used in the document, because I'm not going to give my personal interpretation of that. It wouldn't add anything. The language is pretty clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, for the moment your answer is based on the text of that law, right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So, Mr. Gosnell, if there is an inconsistency in the witness's answer, please direct us to the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't have the reference at my fingertips, Mr. President, so I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But I will ask, Mr. Theunens, if you look at the screen and if you compare the translation on the screen as compared to the translation that you have in your report, you'll see that there's a slight difference. The president of the republic in your report leads the armed forces in peacetime and times of war. In the translation in front of us it says the president of the republic shall head the armed forces in peacetime and war.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you allow for the possibility that there are some nuances of language in respect of determining whether or not someone is a Supreme Commander that you may not fully appreciate. Let's just put it like that.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we go to the top of the document, please. Just the top. I just want to see the ERN. I would like to see the ERN reference. Yeah, I understand. I mean, I used the same reference because what happens sometimes in the OTP is that different documents exist several times in the system and they are translated several times but as an analyst I don't necessarily know that. And here I do note that indeed the language is slightly different. For me, it doesn't make a meaning any different because imagine that Mr. Gosnell was right, then again I would like in the Law on Defence or I would like at the Law on Defence in order to find another article that would identify then who is the Supreme Commander, i.e., who is the most senior political authority to lead the armed forces. In the absence of another article, I think that Article 6 is still valid. And again from looking at the documents and also the -- for example the letter by General Wahlgren, Force Commander of UNPROFOR, to Mr. Hadzic at a later stage complaining about the shelling of civilian locations, is addressed to Mr. Hadzic by Mr. Wahlgren because he considers, I mean Wahlgren considers, Hadzic the supreme or the highest political authority in the RSK. So whether he is leading or heading the armed forces, as far as I am concerned there is no difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's at least establish this. It's true that being the leading political figure does not necessarily mean that you're the Supreme Commander of the armed forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have answered that we would -- sorry. We would have to look at the specific legislation of the country we're referring to. And I don't like an expression like "leading." Maybe it's again a language issue but if you could say -- just say, well, he's the president or is the prime minister, I mean, yeah, let's use official names and then see how the various laws define the competencies and responsibilities of these official -- of these officials.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do items 2, 3, 4, or 5 of Article 6 imply any command and control over the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's not -- no, they don't, Your Honours, because it's explained in item 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Can we go to page -- the next page of your report. You can just flip the page, sir. And if we could please go to Article 34 in the document in front of us. And I'll just pose my question without waiting for it to arrive. Article 34 specifies who is to exercise command and control over the Territorial Defence which, at this time, is defined as the main component of the armed forces. And we see the expression "command and control" is used there very specifically. Now why in your view, and you have expressed some caution as to whether or not you're an expert in this area, and you don't speak B/C/S, and you don't know the political background, but why, to the best of your ability to analyse this, would it say in Article 34 "command and control" and those words wouldn't be used in Article 6?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is because in Article 34 we're talking about the military command and control over the TO based on the political guidance received from the president of the republic as it is defined in paragraph 1 of Article 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I thank you for that answer. But doesn't political guidance to the -- isn't it possible to have a system where political guidance is provided by the political authorities to a Supreme Commander and the political authorities are not the Supreme Commander; isn't that correct, as a matter of military doctrine?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would -- I mean, if we're talking about the RSK as it is in March 1992, because I think that's important, in light of the adoption of another Law on Defence in 1993 and including the introduction of a supreme defence council, if we're talking -- sorry, about the RSK in March 1992, then please show me an article in the law that defines the responsibility of the president differently as I have defined it -- than I have defined it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Am I all right, Mr. President, or is there some guidance from the Bench?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I'll alert you as to what is playing in the back of my mind and what just passed sotto voce between myself and Presiding Judge. That I don't know how far -- how far we're go with this because the -- to the extent that the witness has already explained the limitations of his expertise, isn't the -- apart from the translation issues between B/C/S and English, there is certain constitutional conceptual issues which seem to be wholly outside of the expertise of the witness, and the -- the -- if I might personalise this, I think that you, like myself, know well the difference between effective political control and titular control.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Hall. I really take on board what you said and I agree. The difficulty that we're in is that the report goes into these issues, and I can now provide a transcript reference. Mr. Theunens went into this at pages 4337 and 4339. So I'm in a bit of a dilemma. I accept entirely what you're saying, and yet I somehow need to refute what has been said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But ... I -- I mean, my recollection can be wrong but I think when we discussed this in examination, it was in reference to the letter sent by UNPROFOR General Wahlgren, and this talks about the situation in 1993 and if I'm not wrong that is after the -- the -- adoption of a subsequent Law on Defence of the RSK which talks about the SVK as the armed force of the RSK as well as it introduces the Supreme Defence Council, so we're talking about a different situation. And if I remember well, then I was talking about or I was trying to explain why General Wahlgren sends the letter to Mr. Hadzic. I was not engaging in any legalistic discussion with Mr. Demirdjian at that stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, let's move forward then and try to make progress and get through this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And I'll be guided by the Bench. I understand that I should proceed through and not take too much time trying to get answers that I can't get. So if we could have L49, please. It's a Prosecution document. It's part of the package.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This is an amendment of the 22nd of April, 1993. The important part is on page 3 of the English. It's Amendment 13. And the same word that we saw used in Article 6, at least in one of the translations of Article 6 of the Law on Defence, is again used in amendment 13, and it says: "Leaves the Serbian army of Krajina in times of peace and war in accordance with the RSK constitution and decisions adopted by the Supreme Defence Council and presides over the Supreme Defence Council." Now looking at that, can you agree with me that he is obliged, the president is obliged to follow instructions of the Supreme Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. And he presides over the Supreme Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have L55, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to direct your attention to -- this is the decision to promulgate amendment 8 to the constitution of the RSK dated the 18th of May, 1992. And if we just go around to the top of page 2, it's amendment 8, sub-article 3: "The president of the republic of Serbian Krajina shall appoint the commander of the republic of Serbian Krajina TO and shall appoint and dismiss the presidents, judges, and judge jurors of military courts and military prosecutors." First of all, that appointment presumably would also have to be directed and authorised and decided upon by the Supreme Defence Council. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, because this -- I mean, this is May 1992. The Supreme Defence Council of the RSK is only introduced in April 1993. So this -- we are in a different situation, and I think this is explained even in the amalgamated report, so I would say it's -- it can be very misleading by comparing documents from totally different time-periods with each other. In April 1992, there is no Supreme Defence Council in the RSK.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Okay. That's my mistake and I apologise for that --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. And -- I mean, there is an error in the transcript, and I'm probably speaking too fast. When I say the Supreme Defence Council of the RSK is only introduced in April, I mean April 1993, not 1992. It's a big difference.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: This witness is kindly asked to slow down for the benefit of the interpreters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That's my mistake. But the point that I wanted to make with you or ask you about in respect of this is it says: The president has the power to appoint but there is no power to remove, is there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be good to compare the two texts because if you can appoint, I mean, it should also be explained then who can dismiss if your proposition is correct. If you can -- if you would compare the B/C/S and the English, maybe there's an error in the translation. Or we would try to find another article in the law in this -- in this amendment indicating who then can dismiss because it has to be specified. It has to be put in law who has that authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Can mobilisation be ordered under the Law of All People's Defence by someone other than the SFRY Presidency?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would ask for a more specific question. Which area are we talking about? I mean, which geographic area? What time-period?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I'm just going to -- I'm going move onto another topic and I'm going to come back to that. And I just want to ask you a couple of questions about the situation around Vukovar when it falls. Could we have 00623, please. It's not on our list but this was one of the two that I notified the Prosecution about yesterday. Now this is from Vladimir Stojanovic, the commander of the Guards Motorised Brigade. "I hereby forbid the exchange of SFRY prisoners for the prisoners of the armed formations of the Republic of Croatia without my permission." That's 19th of November, 1991. Does that suggest to you that the JNA considers itself the custodian of all prisoners who have been taken into custody upon the fall of Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, yes, Your Honours. Whereby when we use the word "prisoner," I prefer the language as it is used in paragraph 1 of this document. Actually, I'm very grateful you show it because it's the document I referred to when Mr. Demirdjian was asking me questions about who would you decide about exchange of prisoners and I couldn't recall the exact document, but this is the document that I refer to; that is, that at that moment, i.e., 19th of November, the JNA still wants to centralise any exchange of prisoners of war. And they are defined -- the nature of the prisoners is identified in the document, who these people are.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you know that Aleksandar Vasiljevic visited Vukovar in the 19th of November 1991?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I do, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you know that that is also not recorded in the war diary of the Guards Brigade?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the war diary refers to the arrival of a delegation of senior officers of the security administration. Now, at this moment I don't recall whether this delegation includes General Vasiljevic or it is limited to the three other officers of the security administration, UB.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, I just have two last documents to go through and I think they're highly significant, so we're going to take a little bit of time with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we please go to 1131, Prosecution tab 289.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Is counsel planning to tender the previous document? Because it's not in the package.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that. We would tender that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter document 623 shall be assigned Exhibit D55. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now this document appears to be from the federal secretariat for the National Defence Security Administration. Is Aleksandar Vasiljevic the head of this at this time?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he is still the head at that time because which -- which -- I thought it was May 1992 but maybe I missed it now, the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: The date is the 26th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he has been retired by then. I mean, there was a wave of early retirements and I think that General Vasiljevic was a part of that. But again, I can stand corrected. I haven't looked into his career for the past year. And he has also been held -- or he was arrested at one movement, so he left or he was removed from the security administration at one moment. I also know that he was retired at one moment. I think he was retired already by the date of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: If we turn the page. It's information on the crimes against civilians committed by the members of the paramilitary and the volunteer formations in the RSK. "While carrying out the tasks from within their authorities in the zone of responsibility of the JNA engaged in the territory of the RSK, the organs of the security of JNA gathered a number of operative and other information on the serious criminal acts (murder, theft, abuse, rape, et cetera) committed by the members of the volunteer formations who were, for the most part, on the strength of the TO of Eastern Slavonia, Western Srem, and Baranja at the time those acts were committed. "All information was immediately passed onto the local organs of government, the organs of internal affairs of the Republic of Serbia, and the military-legal organs, and adequate measures on identifying the perpetrators, taking them before the military-legal organs, and documenting all activities were taken." Now just as an initial matter, as you read that, can you see that a distinction is being drawn: On the one hand, information is being disseminated to the local organs of government, the organs of the internal affairs of the Republic of Serbia, as well as military-legal organs, and it says measures are taken to take those cases before the military-legal organs. In other words, doesn't it appear from that that the prosecutions are going to end up before the military-legal organs but that the other agencies or the other identified groups are going to assist in the investigation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I mean, it -- it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: All right. And then on pages 2 and 3, I'm not going to read the discussion there about the events involving Lieutenant-Colonel Dimitrijevic and the Valjevo TO Detachment and the Dusan Silni Detachment in respect of the events described there in Lovas, because that's what it's about, it's about Lovas. And below that description it says: "Handwritten, "1. JNA military prosecutor's office; "2. Republic of Serbia HQ -- republic HQ of Territorial; Defence;" And, 3: "Republic of Serbia under-secretary for State Security Service MUP were informed on the above event in a memo by the security administration of SSNO ..." Now, first of all, would you agree with me that of those the only prosecutorial organ that's notified here is the JNA military prosecutor's office?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And there's no notation that this information should go to any prosecutorial organ in the SBWS; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But then again we come to issue of dates. I haven't seen any documents that by the 26th of October, 1991, there is such a prosecutorial organ or structure in the SBWS bearing also in mind the 1st Military District order 2436-1 from 20th of November, 1991, that, as I mentioned several times, for the first time mentions or identifies the SAO SBWS civilian authorities as competent or relevant organs of civilian authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Theunens, I say that the remaining examples in this report reflect what I've just asked you about so I'm not going to go through it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But I would tender this document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Again, it's part of the package, Your Honours, so we'll note that there's no objection on the admission of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Demirdjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Just one last example, it's D17, Prosecution tab 291.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell, I suppose you will not deal with this document in two, three minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Not likely, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Would it be appropriate to do it after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yes, please, Mr. President. And I would only have ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. And just awareness, Mr. Demirdjian, how long would you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yesterday I announced about 15 to 20 minutes, now I'll say 20 to 25 based on what we heard this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Theunens, we'll take the first break.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: In the remaining time, there is an issue about P171. Mr. Gosnell, that's the -- the one where we had a translation problem. You submitted to the interpreters, and then you said that there was a request for review pending; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That's my information, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes. But is that your request or is that OTP's request?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is our request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So it your request --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was submitted last week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. It is your request and it is with regard to the translation of -- of the word that is translated as "prime minister"; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Because there is another -- another request pending from the Prosecution for which we -- I think we still wait for the answer, or did you give the answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Oh. Your Honours, that was -- yes, let me get back to you after the break. I believe that the issue sorted itself because the version that I had was a non-revised version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Right. Yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: In e-court is the revised version now, so I think that that's closed. That issue is closed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And there is another issue with that same document. It was apparently temporarily put under seal until the Prosecutor advises otherwise. You should deal with this matter as well, Mr. Demirdjian, and tell us whether it should be -- should stay under seal or whether it can go public.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: It is in relation to P171 still.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It's still in relation to P171.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: All right. We will consult during the break, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The Defence will file a motion, I would say, by the end of -- of the week for that revised translation? Would that be possible?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: For this particular document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: This particular document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. And, Mr. Demirdjian, you will tell us after the break about the seal -- under seal or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, I will consult during the break, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, while the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Who's first?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: While the witness is being brought in, I can inform you that Exhibit P171 does not require any protective measures any longer. We have received an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In addition for as to the same exhibit, we did not ask the correction of the translation until last break. It had to be asked on 9 of May, but I apologise for misinformation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Would that mean that we would have to wait a little bit longer to have the review?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It's been asked. It's been asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We asked it during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It's not urgent in that way. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Theunens. Mr. Gosnell, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Could we have D17, please. D17. That's Prosecution tab 291.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, this is a document from the State Security Department centre Belgrade dated the 27th of May, 1992. And it appears to be connected to the previous document we looked at, as it says there -- it refers to information received from the security administration on the -- on the previous day. And then if -- you can just see there that item 1, again, concerns the incidents at the village of Lovas. And if we turn the page to page 2, at the bottom of the discussion about the events in Lovas, it says: "We think that the military prosecutor would have the authority for the possible criminal procedure against these persons." And then if we go to item 4, it says -- it describes an incident in a village called Jankovci. I don't know the location of that. It's not -- it doesn't -- it's not material to my question. And it says: "The conclusion is that the responsibility lies with: Buha Risto as the TO company commander, Carevic, Jovan, a member of the TO, Dragojevic, Petar, also a member of the TO. This action of intimidation ... was carried out on the order of the company commander ... the possible criminal procedure would come under the authority of the military prosecutor's office." Now do you agree that it's very clear when we look at all these examples that it's the opinion of both the SSNO, and here we see a civilian organ, that crimes committed by members of the TO fall within the jurisdiction of military justice for prosecution?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Irrespective of the two documents in -- according to doctrine, it would -- it is correct given the Law on Military Prosecution and the Law on Military Courts of 1977. I just want to highlight that in the document here from the State Security, Serbia, conditional wording is used, i.e., they say that the criminal -- possible criminal procedure would come. I don't know why they write that, you know. I haven't been able to establish. But otherwise I agree with your proposition.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: In most countries, are crimes committed by a member of the armed forces in relation to armed conflict within the exclusive jurisdiction of military justice?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is probably the case. I mean, if we would have to look again as I said earlier to a similar general question to the specific legislation. But as for SFRY, it is clear -- I mean, we discussed those laws.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'm done with that document. Thank you. Now if we could just have a look at two provisions of ... If we could have a look at L10, please. And this is Law on All People's Defence. And I just want to take you briefly to two provisions, if I may. And if we could go to page 11 of the English, which is Article 23. Now there it describes work obligation. Can I just ask you, Mr. Theunens, is -- there's nothing unusual or strange or out of line with prescribing a work obligation for civilian citizens in a time of war in terms of what you know about military doctrine in general?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see these articles in the 1982 All People's Defence law, Your Honours, but I don't remember seeing any JNA documents covering the 1991/1992 conflict in Croatia mentioning work obligation, so there's not much I can say except for reading the article together with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, we're not going to go back to our previous discussion about the entities that are covered by the Law on All People's Defence, but it includes local communes, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does. But of course when it's mentioned in 1982 or any other SFRY law, it refers to recognised entities and recognised local communes. As I mentioned before, the status of some declared entities like the SAOs and their subordinate local structures is a complex matter, and again I have explained how the SFRY political and military leadership tries to handle these things. Another complicating factor is the appearance of these politically affiliated volunteers/paramilitary groups well as groups maintaining special relations with the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia. All these kinds of additional groups and structures were not foreseen in the SFRY legislation, let alone the 1982 All People's Defence law.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Article 71, page 39 in the English. This article is about mobilisation. In the event of an attack on the country or an immediate threat of war or in other emergencies, socio-political communities, self-management organisations and communities, et cetera, shall take and carry out, implement measures and mobilise their forces and resources according to plans for defence." Again -- and then just to go down: "In the event of an attack on the country, communities, organisation, and organs listed in paragraph 1 of this article shall carry out mobilisation even without an explicit order." Would you agree that these communities, whatever may be their legal status, and you have discussed that in your previous answer, would you agree that this mobilisation can occur even without an order from the SFRY Presidency?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the article is clear, but the -- the -- the legal status, i.e., whether these entities are recognised or not is the key provision because otherwise anyone -- I mean, a football club could declare mobilisation but it wouldn't make sense because a football club is not a legally organised entity in the wider concept of All People's Defence, and that is also my understanding of the SAOs, at least initially, until the various additional decisions are adopted during fall 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did the Ministry of Defence of the SBWS have any physical manifestation in the region of the SBWS? Did it have a building? Did it have a telephone? Did it have an office? As far as you know.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to ask for clarification, Your Honours. About which time-period are we talking?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Any time in 1991.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand that a decision is adopted by the Great Assembly concerning the competencies of the Ministry of Defence in -- and this is done in October 1991, but I haven't soon any documents concerning the implementation of this decision and I don't recall other -- as what you call physical manifestations of the existence of the Ministry of Defence of the SBWS in fall 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, thank you very much for your forbearance.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, that concludes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gosnell. Mr. Demirdjian, re-direct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Your Honours, before I commence my re-examination, would this be an appropriate moment to tender the report and the errata sheets if there's no objection?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I suggest that we deal with this at the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's deal with it at the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Demirdjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I will try to be very brief. During the first day of cross-examination if you remember you were asked a number of questions with respect to Arkan's subordination to the JNA. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now there's one document that was shown to you. This is Exhibit D27.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Could we display it on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And if you'll remember, you'll see it in a moment, we will have to go to page 4 in the English version and that is page 8 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now -- so page 4 in English and page 8 in the B/C/S. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now you'll remember that this was a certificate signed by Arkan and you've seen this. There's the header of the TO training centre in Erdut. Now, Mr. Theunens, based on this document, are you able to tell us whether this document was addressed to anyone in specific?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we scroll on the B/C/S to the bottom, please. I mean, the -- it is certificate. There's no specific addressee included. But I know that these kind of certificates were used for -- to -- to support request for compensation, in particular if it concerned somebody who had been injured during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And now this is part of a bundle of about 11 pages I believe. The Defence didn't show you a cover page. Could we put it to page 1 in both versions, please. Mr. Theunens, have you seen this type of form in reviewing documents?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It -- it does remind me to a personnel files of members of the special purpose unit of the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia, I mean the layout, but I'm into the 100 per cent sure, I mean, because those documents I only saw them -- I mean these kind of documents when I testified in the Stanisic/Simatovic trial and I was handed over a CD with documents from the Defence and I believe that similar documents, i.e., personnel files of members of the special unit, the purpose unit of the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia were -- were included in that CD.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now if we go to the next page in both versions under item number 3, "Information on Wounding," you see here under number 2, the date and the place, 2nd of August, during combat operations in Tenja. I think this was covered during your examination-in-chief -- during your cross-examination. And if we now go to the very next page, under item number 4, "Opinion and Conclusion," in the B/C/S version it's a handwritten note, and in the English here we see: "He is living with three other members of his family in a 50 square metre flat. His father is retired. He is unemployed. He has to attend rehabilitation for the next three months. His financial situation is difficult. "Approved assistance of 5.000 dinars," in Belgrade, 16 December 1991. Now there is a name here, assistant Suzana Kerovic. Her position or organisation is not indicated. Again, does this conclusion give you any indication of which institution would have issued this document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't, Your Honour. If it would have been the JNA I would have expected some heading or some stamp from the JNA. But, again, probably there are other documents in the file that may be of assistance in order to clarify this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And have you seen any documents or similar documents which provide financial assistance to wounded or injured, in this case, Arkan members?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Referring again to these personnel files of members of the special purpose is unit of the Ministry of Interior for Republic of Serbia, and these decisions were then issued to the best of my recollection by the competent authorities of the Republic of Serbia and not by the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And are you familiar with the term Captain Dragan Fund, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: What is that, in a nutshell?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not entirely able to answer the question. I know that Captain Dragan kept records.
