I mean, similar documentation of members of volunteer units, whereby some of these people in 1991 were, for example, members of -- of Seselj's volunteers or affiliated with volunteer groups that were linked one way or the other to the SRS or that maintain contact with the SRS war staff, whereby one would see that the same individuals would later identified as members of the special purpose unit of the Ministry of Interior of Republic of Serbia. I understand that this Dragan fund was used, yeah, to regulate requests for compensation for these individuals but I -- that's all can I say about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And a final question on this issue. What system or regulation is provided in the SFRY armed forces with respect to financial assistance to soldiers?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I wouldn't be able to do so because I -- I don't recall that -- having looked at such provisions, I don't believe that it was included in the All People's Defence law, but on the other hand I have included in my report documents concerning the attitude of Republic of Serbia towards volunteers/paramilitaries, and I think that what is what we are talking about here because this is -- discusses a member of a non- -- a unit that was not foreseen in doctrine of All People's Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I'm moving to another topic now at pages 4431 onwards of the cross-examination, if you remember, you were shown a central intelligence agency map of the Eastern Slavonia. I believe this was admitted as Exhibit D38.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: If we could display that on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And while this is coming up, Mr. Theunens, do you remember that you answered -- at least part of your answer was that this map was created based on open-source material; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That -- that is correct. And further details can be found in the -- in the introduction to, I think, part one of this report, "Balkan Battle-Grounds."

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, the Defence asked you whether you would agree that this map accurately represents the units that appeared to be there. And I just warranted to bring your attention to the following. It appears at least in the top right-hand corner here that the letter X refers to a brigade. If we can just zoom on that top right-hand corner there. Yes, do you see the letter X?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. These are the -- the standard symbols like NATO country use -- I'm sorry I touched the screen, but that NATO countries use to depict units on a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. We can zoom out now. And I would like you to --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can we zoom to the central part of this map, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you see in the area of Vinkovci on the right-hand side of the line, you have a 3 Guards Brigade and a 2 Guards Brigade. Have you encountered or have you seen any documents suggesting that such units were deployed in that area? Or employed.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I mean, the potential confusion comes from the fact that there was only one Guards Motorised Brigade in the SFRY armed forces; however, the Proletarian Guards Mechanised Division would also have guards brigades but those were guards mechanised brigades, so there is a difference between the nature of the unit. So there is not necessarily an error in the map but the use of the words "guards" needs to be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. Now after the map was shown to you, you were asked by my learned friend whether the map reflects, if you'll remember, that OG North and OG South were separated, and you answered that it's possible. You can draw your conclusions based on this map, and you can answer it again based on the map you see in front of you. Now, putting aside all these arrows and units that we see on the screen, you did explain during your examination-in-chief - and this was at page 4200 - that the JNA controlled the bridges over the Danube at the three entry points. Do you remember that part of your examination?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, Your Honours. I mean, they start to control them at one moment in time in summer 1991. Or even earlier, I think, late spring 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you -- in view of your answer just now and on the document that you have collected, could you tell the Court what was the level of communication between OG South and OG North?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just to -- do you mean the level of exchange of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, we would have to look at the specific documents because -- I mean, from a doctrinal point of view they should have been in contact with each other because they're neighbouring units. And again given the situation in the area where there are reports of infiltration by members of ZNG and other Croatian forces, it's really imperative that they -- not only that they talk to each other as neighbouring units but there would also be a physical contention, i.e., maybe that they can see each other or that the weapons of the neighbouring units, i.e., north -- OG North, south, OG South, that they can cover the same area to avoid gaps, but I think we would -- I mean, we would have to look at the specific documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Well, on that note, could we display 65 ter 6010 which is at tab 547.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While we're doing it, can we see because I don't remember seeing a date on the map or whether it covers a time-period or not, so -- because that's also important to keep in mind in order to assess the usefulness of this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Perhaps if we're able to display the last document. I don't believe there is a date but let's take a quick look. Perhaps I missed something.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: It'll appear on the legend.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: On the legend. Thank you. Well, if we can zoom on the top right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, I believe you have dates with respect to the boundaries at a certain point in time, and --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, it's -- sorry, I can read. It shows like this -- sorry. I think it's December 1991 so ... I can read this position: Shown as of December 1991 which I would say is of limited use if you want to understand what's happening around Vukovar because by then the Guards Motorised Brigade has been withdrawn and OG South has been disbanded.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So let's look very briefly at 65 ter 6010, please. Yes, I believe we have the English version on the screen. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Theunens, do you see here that this is a document of the command of the 12th Corps on the 6th of October 1991 in the village of Dalj. And I'd like to take your attention to item number 2A: "The command of OG South launched attacks according to a previous decision." And there's a detailed explanation with the involvement of the assault detachments here. Now, this is just one document and there will be more, but can you tell us based on this document on the 6th of October how you would assess the quality of the communities between those two units?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from doctrinal point of view, a unit has to be aware of the activities of a neighbouring unit. I think it's -- the reasons are obvious also given my previous -- my answer to a previous question. Now, again, in the course of military doctrine, this information would be provided by the command of the 1st Military District. There would be regular meetings between -- I mean, held at the command of the military district where commanders or representatives of the commanders of the various subordinate units would be present to receive instructions from the command of the 1st Military District for operations as well as to discuss the situation and there, of course, they would conduct a liaison and during operations they should also be in contact with each other for the reasons I explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a new document. May I apply to tender it, 65 ter 6010.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1720. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I'll move to a different topic, Mr. Theunens. At page 4443 during cross-examination you were shown Exhibit P103, which I would like us to display on the screen now, and this document dealt with, if you'll remember, a report that Arkan had destroyed a Catholic church in the village of Erdut. Thank you. Now at the bottom of the page we see the sentence there -- this is the document of the 1st of October 1991 from the security organs of a military unit -- yes. And at the bottom of the sentence here, do you see the sentence, the last three lines, and it read -- and I'm going to read it slowly for you: "Arkan had completely destroyed a Catholic church in the village of Erdut and the church tower was destroyed before that, during the JNA's takeover of Erdut." Now, during your cross-examination, the Defence asked you whether you were disputing that the last sentence on page 1 referred to the takeover of Erdut on the 1st of August by the JNA. Looking at the document - and I'd like to bring your attention to the word "and" in the middle of that sentence - what is your view with respect to the incidents that are being referred to here?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to understand the purpose of the comma between "that" and "during," because I think that would -- I mean, I haven't -- I don't have any other or any specific recollection as to when the church was destroyed. I have a recollection that the tower was destroyed during the takeover because there were allegedly ZNG members hiding in it, and -- to -- to which were considered threat by the JNA. But I have no specific recollection as to when Arkan destroyed the church. So that's all can I say it is -- I mean, you could say that it was after the takeover, but the comma is in my view is misleading. So I can't answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: All right. I'll move onto the next topic, Mr. Theunens. If you'll remember during your cross-examination this was at pages 4463 onwards, you were asked within the context of the events in SBWS when do combat operations end in OG North. Do you remember that question?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And you answered that your interpretation of the documents led you to conclude that the JNA had taken control of Dalj on August 1st. I want you to take a look at Exhibit P1690, which is at tab 544 of the Prosecution list. Again, this is a document of the Command of the 12th Corps on the 28th of September, 1991. Under the first header you see that Colonel Belic is appointed commander of the operations group. And I'd like to take your attention to item number 2: "The OG commander is tasked with consolidating forces north of Vukovar, blocking exit from Vukovar from the north and preparing to lift the siege of Vukovar." Could you tell us, based on this document and other documents that you have seen, what is the mission of OG North at that stage, at the end of September 1991?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Objection. That's vague, very vague, given the composition of OG North.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I'm trying to be as non-leading as possible in this stage. I'm focussing on the information we have in this document with respect to what OG North is being assigned with.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if the question refers to the OG North that is discussed in this order, well, I think the paragraph is clear. It's to prevent Croatian forces from exiting Vukovar via the north. Also -- I mean, consolidating forces means that you extend your control, your -- I mean, your -- finalise your deployment and then you're ready to operate while deployed in the area north of Vukovar which is the -- I mean, the area is not specified but it's north of Vukovar. And I spoke about blocking the exit, I mean preventing forces -- Croatian forces from exiting or from leaving Vukovar via the north. And then also assisting the other JNA forces in lifting the siege -- what is called the siege of Vukovar, i.e., by the parts in Vukovar that are under Croatian control.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And if you look at the bottom of this document at item 7, it talks about the command of the 12th Corps being responsible to provide logistical support. And then item number 8 which says: "Relocate the command post to the sector of the village of Borovo Selo." Now what does that tell you with respect, again, to my earlier question of the mission or perhaps the focus of OG North at the time?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, overall, I mean, the geographic focus is north of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And might I show you one more document on this issue, which is at 65 ter 6016, at tab 552. Mr. Theunens, this is one of the new documents, and this is with respect to the formation of a tactical group. We discussed this during your examination-in-chief. It is issued by the Command of the 12th Corps on the 9th of October, 1991. Could you look at the first sentence: "Order. "To unify operations of all forces engaged in the attack on Borovo Naselje in Borovo and to ensure further completion of planned tasks ...," and then we see the order itself. You know, with respect to the last document we saw. In light of the content of that last document, what is your view of the -- again, the focus of OG North or TG North at the time?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for this order, it -- I mean, it's specified in the first sentence. It's Borovo Naselje, which is actually between Borovo Selo and Vukovar, and I would say that this corresponds with the area -- I mean, generally speaking the area in order -- north-west of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a new document. May I apply to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1721. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I'll move onto my next topic, Mr. Theunens. You were asked -- you were shown exhibit -- sorry. 65 ter 460 you were shown yesterday, I believe. And it was with respect to an order from Zivota Panic to send a number of units including the Vojvodina TO. And at the time the Defence pointed to you that there was no mention of the SBWS TO in this order. Yes, we can see it on the screen right now. And you explained in response that at the time the local Serb TO in SBWS was not recognised and that's how you explained the absence of a mention of the SBWS TO here. Now, are you able to assist the Trial Chamber, based on the amount of documents you have seen with respect to the operations in Vukovar, for what purpose were the local Serb TO used during the combat operations?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, there is an order from OG South, if I remember well it's the number 235-1 from the 14th of October, where it is stated that TO Petrova Gora and Leva Supoderica are to be used as guides which makes sense because the local -- members of the local Serb TO, i.e., those originating from the area, know the area better than the members of the Guards Motorised Brigade and this is particularly important in the context of urban warfare as it was by that time in the outskirts of Vukovar. From other documents, just summarising them, we also see that the TO is used to control the terrain, i.e., the rear area, because the JNA units of -- are used on the front line. I mean, those are the main missions I remember at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You anticipated my next question, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And, on that note, if we could display on the screen 65 ter 353, which is at tab 92 of the Prosecution's list.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, you see on the screen that this is a document issued by the Guards Motorised Brigade Command on the 1st of October, 1991, command post in Negoslavci. Do you see that on the screen?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, just to place us back in the context, when did the Guards Motorised Brigade arrive in the area of Negoslavci?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, end of September 1991, early October. Because -- I mean, the resubordination order which is discussed on page 442 dates from the 29th of September. By this resubordination order the Guards Motorised Brigade is resubordinated from the SSNO to the 1st Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So this would be have been -- am I correct to say that this is about a day or two days later after the arrival of the Guards Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. And it's, in my recollection, one of the first orders by the Commander of the Guards Motorised Brigade for operations of his unit in the wider Vukovar area and at that time Colonel Mrksic is not yet the commander for OG South.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can I take you to page 2 in the English version. We can remain on the same page in the B/C/S version. Yes. Now, you see here -- I apologise. There's a mention here to the Leva and Desna Supoderica and --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can we scroll down a little bit more, please. I apologise. I may have had the wrong version of the document. Can we go to the next page. Can we scroll down a little bit more. Just give me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah. And maybe I can use this to -- sorry, to correct my -- the order, I was referring to 235-1, is not from the 14th of October, but it's the 29th of October and this is discussed on page 457 of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. It appears that my handwriting was playing tricks on me too, as my learned friend earlier today. It is page three. At the bottom of that page, please. Look, we are there. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you see the paragraph here? It says: "Bring up infantry sections at the achieved line during the night before first light on 2 October with guides from Petrova Gora ... TO detachment." Now, is this what you were referring to earlier with respect to the use of local Serb TO?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. And I -- excuse me. Indeed, Your Honours. And I have explained why the Guards Motorised Brigade was doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, the paragraph before that, paragraph 2, suggests -- well, it says: "The Gmtbr will conduct a blockade and assault on Vukovar." And in the seconds line it says: "In co-operation with Vukovar TO units (Petrova Gora) ..." Now, I'd like you to explain to the Trial Chamber, if you're able to form a view, as to how the Guards Motorised Brigade arriving on the 29th or 30th of September would have established a contact with the local Serb TO in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I haven't seen specific documents on that, but, again, from a doctrinal point of view, there would have been meetings between the members of the -- I mean, the relevant members of the Guards Motorised Brigade, i.e., members of the command, battalion commander, company commanders, and commanding officers of local Serb TO unit -- units, I'm sorry, in the respective areas or zones of responsibilities of the companies, the battalions of the Guards Motorised Brigade. So there would be meetings at the level of the command as well as at the the lowest unit level so that everybody knows everybody and that they can also co-ordinate their operations in view of conducting operations, I mean, and implementing the three principles of command and control.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. I'll move onto my penultimate topic. I believe it is yesterday, at page 4589, that you were shown Exhibit D48.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: If we could have that up on the screen, please. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You'll remember that the Defence were asking as to why these appointments here are being made by -- at the SSNO level. If you remember that was the question yesterday. And we see a number of colonels, lieutenant-colonels, six of them in fact, that are being assigned to the towns of Mirkovci and Tenja. And you answered that if they came outside the 1st Military District, then that could have been an explanation as to why it's the SSNO that issues that order because the 1st Military District cannot order officers, et cetera. Now, I'd like you to look at one of the new documents. It's at 65 ter 6074.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document was not on our list. I believe that it might assist in answering the witness, his request basically to see a document about the appointment of the officers. So 65 ter 6074.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I haven't even had sight of the document. I mean ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, and I agree. It's not on our list but it arose from the witness's answer yesterday, and I believe it would help the witness in forming his view why this document was issued by the SSNO. This is not a topic that we appreciated would be raised in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I -- I don't like to be technical, Mr. President, but if this was known yesterday we should have received an e-mail last night or this morning, and having not even had ten minutes to look at the document, much less consult, I object to its use.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I'm in your hands Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I would think that Mr. Gosnell has a point there, Mr. Demirdjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I -- I agree, Your Honours. But, again, if further cross-examination is necessary after the break I would have no objection to that. Again, I'm in your hands. If it assists you to help complete --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Would that solve the problem eventually, Mr. Gosnell?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It's your call.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'm extremely loathe to suggest that any further questions on my part would be something anyone in this room would appreciate, so I would suggest it's not an available or appropriate remedy and we should just not use this document and move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Well, I would not object to additional questions. But if we're down to that, I can move, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please ask your question without showing the document, if that's appropriate or relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yeah. It would be very difficult for Mr. Theunens to answer the question without seeing the document and the appointments made. It's not a major issue, Your Honours. I will move on. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: This morning, Mr. Theunens - and this is my last topic, it is - at page 18, line 13, you were asked by my learned friend, or you were told that none of the documents that you have reviewed at all show that the district was involved in ethnic cleansing or putting pressure on Croats to leave. Do you remember that question?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I would like you to look at Exhibit D51 which the Defence showed you during their cross-examination. We see here the cover page from the Command of the 1st Mechanized Corps. And this document is sent to the 1st Military District. I would like you to go to page 4 in the English version, which is page 3 in the B/C/S version. And if we could zoom on item number 10 which was shown to you by my learned friend. Sir, in the middle of this paragraph, do you see the sentence that starts with the word "because"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In -- in paragraph 10 or is --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, item 10, line 6: "Because of distrust and what is happening to Serbs who remain in Western Slavonia ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And the sentence continues: "And with the tacit consent of the government of the SAO Slavonia and the assistance of the prominent members of the government, the so-called co-ordinators and ministers, they are placing a certain pressure on the local inhabitants to make them move out voluntarily." Now, sir, with respect to the question that was asked this morning in the documents you have reviewed, what is your view with respect to the involvement of the Serbian district?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have answered that question but I can repeat it and I will try to be as brief as possible. That is that based on my review of JNA documents, a pattern develops whereby pressure is exercised on members of the population. This consists mainly of minority members of the population, even of ethnic groups that were not directly involved in the conflict. I remember seeing a document concerning -- sorry, a JNA document with a need to protect Ruthenians and Ukrainians, but they were not a faction or a party in the conflict between Croatian forces and JNA forces and related forces under the latter's command, and this pattern consists of, yeah, pressure, whereby this is condoned or even supported or there's even active involvement of people affiliated with the SAO SBWS government or even members of that government. And this pattern continues also after the official withdrawal of JNA in spring 1992 and the latter conclusion is based on the reports by the UN Secretary-General on the implementation or the resolutions regulating the activities of the UN peacekeeping forces, UNPROFOR, in -- in the UNPAS in view of the implementation of the Vance Plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, we've seen one document which was tendered by the Defence. Allow me to show you one last document, I promise. It is 65 ter 6145 at tab 634. This is a document of the 19th of March of the 1st Mechanized Corps, and I would like you to go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, in all fairness to the Defence, this is a document they did object to during my examination-in-chief with respect to the involvement of the Serbian district. However, my learned friend has dealt with that issue now in his cross-examination, and I would like to use this document at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, do you see here at the top of the page under item number 6, Novica Gusic, who we have seen writing numerous reports from the 1st Mechanized Corps writes again: "The moving out of the local population is being organised by the local civilian authorities with supervision and security provided by the IS/expansion unknown/of the government of the SO Baranja, Eastern Slavonia, and Western Srem. The person in charge is Ziko Vevcevic." And again, Mr. Theunens, how does that compare with the document we just saw, the previous document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, Your Honours, this document is consist with the previous document and the others, other documents I reviewed which led me to draw the conclusion concerning the pattern I have identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you for answering my questions, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1722. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: This concludes my re-examination, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Demirdjian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Expert Witness Theunens, I have one last question for you. It concerns the Supreme Command of the armed forces and its decisions in the territory concerned. You remember at the beginning of your testimony, I asked you a question about the Supreme Command of the armed forces of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, or, as we call it - I'm looking for the acronym in English - SFRY. And you explained very well that the Supreme Command of the armed forces of the SFRY consisted of the Presidency which, in turn, was comprised of the presidents -- no, the president of the League of Communists of Yugoslavia and delegates from the six republics and the two autonomous provinces. Now, regarding the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia with its constitution of 1972, the Supreme Command over the army is in the hands of the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the presidents of republics. So there is a difference. What attracted my attention is the collective nature of this Supreme Command. The president always acts with the consent of the delegates from republics. Can you tell me, based on your research and studies and your expertise, whether you have found in any of the documents, such as transcripts from their sessions, the sessions of the Supreme Command of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, or perhaps those of the republics, whether you found any documents bearing on JNA actions or operations, or perhaps the new army of the new Federal Republic of Yugoslavia called the VJ, any operations concerning the district of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, or the Serbian Republic of Krajina in the period between 1991 and 1993? In other words, were you able to see in your research that the authorities of the geographic area concerned by the indictment participated in the decision-making concerning the involvement of the JNA in these activities and the activities of the paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I think your question, if I understood it well, covers several aspects. Starting with the last aspect, i.e., the presence of members of -- of local Serb authorities be it in Croatia or Bosnia-Herzegovina, I do remember seeing some documents concerning sessions of I would call it what remains of the SFRY Presidency from spring 1992. I call it what remains of the SFRY Presidency because by that time obviously the representatives of Slavonia and Croatia are not part anymore of the SFRY Presidency, and in these documents, I mean, they mention the presence of Mr. Martic and/or Mr. Karadzic, and I believe - but I would need to see the document - I also believe Mr. Hadzic. These documents or these sessions of what remains of the SFRY Presidency concern the preparation of the territory covered by the SAOs and subsequently the RSK in Croatia for the deployment of the UN peacekeeping forces which includes, I mean, the various aspects concerning again preparing the JNA for its withdrawal, the creation of -- or the formalisation, the formal creation of a RSK TO and related issues. At the same time, I think the other aspect of your question concerns orders concerned -- by the SFRY Presidency and later the FRY Presidency on the activities of the JNA and subsequently the VJ in the SAOs and subsequently the RSK. I have also seen such documents whereby I think the focus there was mainly -- I mean, the various minutes, the focus is mainly on the provision of support to the local Serb defence structures and also, for example, General Panic highlights the dependency of the local Serb defence structures on the assistance from FRY by that time. I mean, after April 1992. We also saw that during at least one session the participation of volunteers/paramilitaries in the conflict in Bosnia-Herzegovina in April May 1992 is being discussed, and this is interested in the context of your question because these are similar groups as those or even the same groups as those that were active in the area covered by the SAO SBWS in fall 1991. So I'm not sure whether I covered each of the aspects you raised in your question, but these are at least the documents concerning the activities of the SFRY and subsequently FRY Presidency I recall. And maybe just to complete, I don't recall seeing, for example, that members of the SAO leadership or local Serb authorities in Croatia or Bosnia-Herzegovina -- I mean, I -- I -- that -- I mean, they cannot impose decisions on what the JNA or they cannot impose their views as what the JNA should be doing or not be doing or what later the VJ should be doing or not be doing, because as you say the decisions are taken in a collegial manner. But for spring 1992, there I do recall documents where members of local Serb authorities are present and also expressed certain views. But I -- it is -- I don't recall the extent to which their views were dominating or -- or prevailing in the decision-making process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, expert Witness. You have, indeed, answered my entire question. Thank you for taking the trouble to answer additional questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I have two questions -- two questions of you. Could we have document with 65 ter number 500 on the screen, please. This document with this -- which is signed by Momir Talic is about engagement of and co-ordination with TO units in the zone of responsibility of the 5th Corps. What I would like to know is: What is or what was in late 1991 the zone of responsibility of the 5th Corps; do you know? And with zone of responsibility, I'm referring to the geographical zone.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, by that time the 5th Corps is the main JNA unit conducting operations in Western Slavonia, and they have been redeployed due to the events -- I mean, the headquarters which prior to the events in Croatia was in -- in -- in Zagreb has been redeployed by that time to Banja Luka in Bosnia-Hercegovina, so they are basically covering the area -- covered western Bosnia-Herzegovina and fighting in -- in Western Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And the second question is about uniforms, Mr. Theunens. I don't know if you know about the uniforms of the different parts of the Serbian forces engaged in the region. Are there elements by which uniforms of JNA regular conscripts on one hand and reservists on the other? Military police, TO, and paramilitary can be distinguished by, let's say, observant ordinary people? I don't have whether you have that information in your documents, but ...

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I -- I don't have any pictures, I think, included in my reports on the uniforms, but I think I can provide some assistance I hope. The JNA traditional uniform was an olive-drab uniform. One single colour. And the most distinct mark was the red cross -- oh, no, sorry, the red star, not the cross, the star on the helmet or on the little cap they were wearing. Military police would be distinguishable because they wear white belts. To my recollection, TOs - I mean the official TOs - would wear similar uniforms. Also, if you notice that the Guards Motorised Brigade - and I'm not sure whether this was already at the outset of their presence in Vukovar or during their operations in Vukovar, but they received or they started to wear camouflage uniforms which were quite unique at that time for the JNA forces operating in Croatia. And then, of course, the big problem were the volunteers and paramilitaries whereby they were often wearing a mixture of JNA and other uniforms, whatever they could find. They would wear party insignia be it on caps. I mean, like Seselj's volunteers, for example, some of them would wear fur caps with the Chetnik symbol on it or they would wear these symbols on other parts of the uniform. At the same time you have the Arkan -- or members of Arkan's group which were seen in camouflage uniform but they are all the same uniform. I mean, very disciplined impression compared to at least what we saw in the local Serb TO. And they would also have a -- often an insignia on their shoulders indicating their allegiance. They wouldn't have any Yugoslav symbols. Some reference is made to -- in documents to Arkan's volunteers wearing black uniforms or black overalls. I remember seeing that myself when I visited Erdut in 1990 -- in August 1993. And for the later period, I mean, after April 1992, the SVK -- excuse me, the RSK TOs officially demobilised but you still see people in mixture of uniforms in the area covered by the RSK. At the same time then there is also the PJM, so the special police, and they wear blue tiger stripe uniforms which was a very distinct feature. And then when the SVK is established in -- after November 1992 - I mean formally established, the law dates from May 1992 but the actual implementation is after November 1992 - they wear camouflage uniforms with again an SVK insignia on the shoulder. But the big problem is for the volunteers and paramilitaries except Arkan and Dragan, of course, but the others they wear a mixture of uniforms and insignia, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Theunens. Anything triggered by the Judges' questions? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With regard to the transcript, there's something I would like to point out. There's some mistakes that have been made with regard to what I said. When I said the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, for example, and I can see that in the transcript it says the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. When I spoke about federal republic I see it says the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. So I'm saying this for the sake of the transcript. And then with regard to the constitution of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, I see that there's a mistake in relation to the date mentioned. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, this brings us to the end of your testimony. Thank you very much for assisting the Tribunal. You are now released as a witness and we wish you a safe journey home or wherever you go to right now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: As for the expert report and the documents, unless there is no objection for the -- from the Defence, the Trial Chamber would like to have written submissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Certainly no objection from us, Mr. President. No objection to that procedure at all.
