utterances.text: So which means that you will object to the admission and -- of documents and report? Is that -- is that correct understanding?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I -- I can say there will be an objection to some of the documents, that's for sure. I think there is still further consultation required before I can take a position on the report itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we will wait for your written submissions. Yes, Mr. Demirdjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can I just get a clarification as to whether there will be submissions both on the report and the documents? Is there an objection to -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Well, I heard a yes for the documents, there will be.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And a maybe for the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. And for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: That's right, isn't it, Mr. Gosnell?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That's quite correct. Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And with respect to the documents, Your Honours, I don't know how we could do this but it would be very helpful if we had an indication of what is being objected to at this stage in order for us to provide you with you a reasoned submission --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: That's one of the reasons why we are asking for written submissions, Mr. Demirdjian. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- I suppose that will happen that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I apologise for intervening, Mr. President. Last week, and maybe we're talking about a separate batch of documents, I believe that we received guidance from the Trial Chamber that the parties were going to confer and that the Defence was going to identify documents to which it objected. And then once that -- the parties had conferred and documents had been identified to which there is objection, then that product would come to the Chamber, and I had the impression that it was -- that proposal had been warmly received by the Chamber. I don't know whether we're being told something different now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Certainly not, Mr. Stringer. The Trial Chamber is always in favour of discussion between parties before taking official positions. Thank you. We'll take the break and come back, let's say, 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: We have a new witness, I take.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. The new witness is being brought in. And just for the record to note now Ms. Lisa Biersay in with the Prosecution together with legal intern, Ivana Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Good afternoon, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You can hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us your name, your date of birth, and your ethnicity, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Goran Stoparic. The 17th of January, 1968. I am of Serbian ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. You are about to make the solemn declaration, by which witnesses commit themselves to tell the truth, and I have to point out to you that by doing so you expose yourself to the penalties of perjury should you give false or untruthful information to the Tribunal. Can I please ask you to write -- to read the solemn declaration now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stoparic, also for coming to The Hague to assist the Tribunal. You may be seated. Ms. Biersay, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Stoparic.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And I see you adjusting. Are you comfortably seated, or is there something we can do with the chairs to assist?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Everything's fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you recall, Mr. Stoparic, giving a statement to investigators from this Tribunal in November of 2003?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And did you sign that statement on 24 November 2003?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that you have provided additional statements to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And you've also previously testified before this Tribunal; correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: On a number of occasions.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Stoparic, I apologise in advance to you and the interpreters who have to listen to my cough. I'm very sorry about that. Turning now to the 2003 statement, in that statement you describe your deployment as a volunteer in the former Yugoslavia; correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Turning now to tab 1, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: May we have 65 ter number 5977 displayed for Mr. Stoparic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And, first, when it comes I'll ask to you look at the right side of your screen. So now directing your attention to the right side of your screen which is a -- an English document, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What do you recognise it to be?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: That's my statement from 2003, I believe, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And directing your attention to the bottom of that page, do you recognise a signature at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Yes. I can recognise my own signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now if we could turn to page 23 of the English version. If we could go one more -- right. On the right, I now have the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: We're trying to get you the right page the -- of the English. Okay. Now on the right of your screen, do you see a signature that you recognise on page 23 of the English version?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And whose signature do you recognise that to be?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: It's mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: In a minute, I will ask for tab 11, which is 65 ter number 6329.1.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And that's just a reference to the -- to the Court, Mr. Stoparic. And now directing my attention to you, Mr. Stoparic, I'd like you to summarise your relevant whereabouts from summer of 1991 to the end of 1993, to orient the Trial Chamber specifically on a map. And I'll ask you to mark that map.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And if we can give some assistance to Mr. Stoparic in that regard. And now turning to tab 11, 65 ter number 6329.1. And, for the record, it is a map of the southeast part of Croatia with a bit of north-west Serbia depicted.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So, Mr. Stoparic, I thought what we could do here is for you to mark and number each place that you've been to and I'll ask you the specific questions in that regard. Now, you describe in your November 2003 statement that in summer 1991 you were in Sid, Serbia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's where I live.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And could you please draw a circle.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: It's Sid.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: We're conferring because we are hearing another interpretation in our headphones. Just one minute. Let's try it again. Could you now draw a circle around Sid and put a number 1 next to it, please.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And could you write number 1 next to -- just outside of that circle, if you can. I know it's tricky with that pen.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: From Sid you went to Tovarnik, Croatia, according to your statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask my colleague to avoid leading questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is covered in his statement. I'm merely trying to be efficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And now, Mr. Stoparic, if you could draw a circle around Tovarnik. If can you see it.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And -- exactly. You've numbered it number 2. Could you describe to the Trial Chamber in what capacity you went to Tovarnik?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Well, I was a volunteer in the Territorial Defence of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: To what JNA brigade was that Territorial Defence of the SBWS attached in Tovarnik?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: At the time, there was a motorised brigade from Kraljevo but I don't know its number. It was the Motorised Kraljevo Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: From Tovarnik you went to Ilaca, Croatia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Could you please draw a circle around Ilaca, writing number 3 to it, please.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: In what capacity did you go to Ilaca?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: In the same capacity as in the case of Tovarnik. I was a member of the Territorial Defence of the SBWS, or, rather, I was a volunteer for that body.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And for the record, Ilaca, I-l-a-c-a. From Ilaca, Mr. Stoparic, you went to Djeletovci; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And could you now please draw a circle around Djeletovci, writing number 4.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And in what capacity did you go to Djeletovci?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Yet again, I was a volunteer within the Territorial Defence of the SBWS.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And do you recall approximately when you were in Djeletovci, on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: It was probably at the beginning of September, but I don't know exactly. I've forgotten.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: From Djeletovci you then went to Lipovaca in Serbia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now I know that Lipovaca is not on the map. Are you able to locate it, drawing an X in the approximate area.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And could you draw the number, I believe we're now at number 5, next to that X.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And in what capacity were you in Lipovaca?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Well, we were still volunteers for the TO of SBWS there. However, we were provided with training. The volunteers were brought up to strength. And then we were renamed. In fact, we were told we would be under the command of the Guards Brigade. It would no longer be called the Kraljevo Brigade. We would no longer be under the Kraljevo Brigade. And then we were to be sent to Vukovar. That's what was said.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And from Lipovaca, Serbia, where did you go next?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Our next destination was Vukovar, or to be more precise, Petrova Gora. First went to Velepromet and -- well, that, in fact is Petrova Gora.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: When you were in Vukovar, in what capacity were you operating?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: In Vukovar, we joined the Leva Supoderica detachment or unit. And as a detachment, we were under the command of the Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stoparic. Just one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I just looked up and saw that we -- but it's not operative; is that correct? The private ... okay.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is correct. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Stoparic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Why is that on, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: That's a good reason. It's broken.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, could you now draw a circle around Vukovar numbering it, I believe that we are now at number 6.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What was your position within the Leva Supoderica?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Well, first we arrived at Velepromet where we were issued with new uniforms and we were taken to Nova Ulica from there. That was the name of the place, Nova Ulica, or New Street.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did you have a specific role with respect to Leva Supoderica? Did you have a title?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: For the first three days I was the commander of a detachment, and then up until the end of the war I was a platoon commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And over --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: I was first a squad commander and subsequently a platoon commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: When you were a platoon commander, over how many squads did you have responsibility?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Well, there were three squads, I think. Between 38 and 40 men I would say.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And when you say "38 to 48 [sic] men," do you mean in each squad or total.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: In total. In the platoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, after Vukovar you were deployed to Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: I was in Bosnia and Herzegovina as a volunteer for the Serbian Radical Party, which was also under the command -- it was also under the command of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I won't ask you to mark that. Now, after Bosnia and Herzegovina you returned to Sid; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Yes. I returned to Sid.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And could you put a number 7 next to the number that's already there for Sid, which was your starting point.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: After Sid, you went to Djeletovci again; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. I was then a member of the Skorpions unit and their base was in Djeletovci. But I also went to Bosnia with that unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And at this time could you write, please, the number 8 next to the number that you already have for Djeletovci.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, you describe that you were deployed to -- with the Skorpions to Bosnia and Herzegovina. Could you, in a very summary fashion, tell the Trial Chamber where you went after leaving Djeletovci, Croatia?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Well, we went to two areas in Bosnia and Herzegovina. We went to the Bihac battle-field and the other battle-field was the Trnovo battle-field in the vicinity of Sarajevo, in the surroundings of Sarajevo. In fact, there were three areas. There was another one in Velika Kladusa in Cazinska Krajina, the Cazin Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And after Bosnia, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Well, after Bosnia, I went to Djeletovci again and then to Sid and then I was in the JSO reserve force. We returned to the Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem again. But that was prior to the Erdut Agreement, and we weren't engaged in combat activity of any kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Could you explain what you mean by "JSO reserve force." What does JSO stand for? If you -- if you know.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Well, the JSO is a special unit. They used to call them or they would usually call that unit the Red Berets. And I went from Sid to Tara to Hotel Amerika. We were provided with significant training there, and we were then sent onto Krajina from there. Or, rather, to Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. The JSO was also a unit that belonged to the state security of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: When did you end your military career?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: It was in Kosovo in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: At this time, the Prosecution would tender both the marked version of 65 ter number 6329.1 as well as the unmarked version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The 65 ter document 6329.1 unmarked map shall be assigned Exhibit P1723. And the marked version of this document shall be assigned Exhibit P1724. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Stoparic, I'd like to go back to your 2003 statement. So if we could go back to tab 1, 65 ter 5977. Now, regarding your November 2003 statement, in preparation for your testimony in the Stanisic and Simatovic case in December of 2010, you had an opportunity to review the statement in your own language; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And based on your review, an amendment to this 2003 statement was prepared in order to make it more accurate; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You made some corrections to the November 2003 statement, and that -- those corrections were recording -- recorded in a separate document and submitted for your review; correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now if we could please turn to tab 2. 65 ter number 5976, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, this is a bilingual document. Do you recognise this document, Mr. Stoparic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what do you recognise it to be?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Well, those are the amendments that I made.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And if we could scroll to the bottom of that page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you recognise the initials at the end of that document?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Yes. They are my initials.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now for the record --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: This is not directed at you, Mr. Stoparic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: For the record this amendment also covers some corrections to a 2005 statement which is not relevant for these proceedings. There's a second page to this document. Could we please see it. And scrolling to the bottom of this page 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you recognise the initials on that page?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And whose initials do you recognise them to be?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Stoparic, in relation to this case, the Hadzic case, you again reviewed your November 2003 statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And did you have some additional corrections that you wanted made to that statement?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I think there were no corrections to make.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Well, perhaps the word "correction" is not the appropriate word.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Could we turn back to tab 1. 65 ter 5977. And if we could now go to the second page in the -- the English. Specifically going to paragraph 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: In paragraph 6, Mr. Stoparic --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: If we could look at the B/C/S version. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: It describes that you joined the volunteers sometime in July of 1991. Regarding the July date, is there anything that you'd like to modify?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was probably the end of August or the beginning of September. I'm wrong about -- I was wrong about July. That's too early.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And now I'd like to direct your attention to paragraph 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And the B/C/S -- yes, it's there as well. In paragraph 7, it would be page 3 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You say "TO volunteer," which TO are you referring to in paragraph 7?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Well, at that time the Territorial Defence of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem was established. I mean that TO. It's simply shorter to say just "TO" but I refer to TO SBWS.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And now if we could turn to paragraph 9.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Towards the end of that paragraph, the -- the third sentence before the end, it starts: "We were subordinated ..." Do you see that sentence, Mr. Stoparic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So it reads: "We were subordinated to the 1st Guards Brigade of the JNA." And this is in reference to your time in Tovarnik. Are there any modifications that you'd like to make to that sentence?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was my mistake. It should read a brigade from Kraljevo. We were not under the Guards Brigade at that time. So I was wrong saying the Guards Brigade. I should have said "a brigade" or "the brigade from Kraljevo."

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And now if we could turn to paragraph 17, which is on page 4 of the English. I believe 6 of the B/C/S. 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: The third line, it says: "We were withdrawing from Krajina ..." And I wondered if you could describe to the Trial Chamber what you mean by "Krajina" in that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Well, that's the district of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. I always referred to it as Krajina, for short. But there was also a Knin Krajina. I usually call them Krajina, but I mean the district of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now turning to paragraph 32, which I believe is B/C/S, 9, page 9, and English page -- also 9. Oh, excuse me, it's 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: In this paragraph, Mr. Stoparic, you refer to the -- the saving of what's described as a member of the ZNG Croatian National Guard called Damir Lorenzo. Do you see that name?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Yes. However, I described here the incident where he was abused a little and then rescued, and I thought he was called Damir Lorenzo. However, three years ago I was watching on the Internet a trial before this Tribunal and I saw a man from Croatia, Captain Velin Karlovic, and I recognised him. So it's not Damir Lorenzo. It's that Veljko Karlovic. And I heard him, watching the trial, describe the same event.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now directing your attention to paragraph 52 --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Which is page 11 in the English. And perhaps ...

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I know that you corrected this in a 2005 statement, Mr. Stoparic. But because we're using the 2003 statement, we have to address it here. Directing your attention to paragraph 52.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Well, it says at some point I visited the camp in Buna in Podvelezje where volunteers of the radical party were. Actually, I was never there. That's what I corrected. I have never been there.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And now directing your attention to paragraph 75, which in English is on page 15. Specifically, I'd refer you to the last part of that sentence. Can you see it in your own language on the screen, Mr. Stoparic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know. I remember. Here I corrected this part where I joined the Skorpions. There were 200 men. I thought 30 per cent were without experience, 30 per cent were experienced, and 30 per cent were undergoing training in Kula and Tara. What is written here is "Frenki's Red Berets." No, that was not the case. They were just sent there for training. That's where the mistake is. What it says here is "directly from the Red Berets," which is not true. Our men went there for training.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Stoparic, with those modifications that you've just made, in light of the 2010 amendment, if the Trial Chamber considers your 2003 statement in conjunction with the 2010 amendment and the modifications you've made here, would they have an accurate and truthful account of your evidence?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: The Chamber would have a reflection of my testimony which, as far as I know, is truthful and accurate. That is what I have experienced.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd now like to ask you some additional questions, Mr. Stoparic. First, regarding paragraphs 6 and 41 of your statement, you discuss the nationalist idealogy and propaganda that was happening in the former Yugoslavia in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I would now like to play for you what is at tab 94. 65 ter number 470.1, and it's a clip from 16 minute and 50 seconds to 17 -- we won't start it just yet -- to 17 minute, 34 seconds. And it is from the BBC documentary, "The Death of Yugoslavia." And this is -- the specific clip that's being played is believed to have been during the early part of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: "To this end, extremist allies of President Milosevic set about provoking a conflict between the Serbs and Croats."

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did you recognise the speaker?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's Dr. Vojislav Seselj, president of the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Have you ever met him in person?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Yes, in Sid. We did not talk on that occasion, but we shook hands when he visited, and for a while I was a member of that party.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And now --

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: But we talked here in the courtroom. That's where we got to know each bother better.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And by that you mean in the Seselj case?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd now like to direct your attention to this clip pertaining to Plitvice in April of 1991. And it's tab -- tab 97. 65 ter 4990.1.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: "THE INTERPRETER: [Voiceover] The Serbian people live here. This is Serbian land. And will forever remain Serbian. Since the decision about establishing the SBWS, he called historic, Dr. Seselj said the following: This, you are the people who are supposed to defend Serbian borders. He promised that nobody -- Serbs in Croatia will not be left on their own. You are heroically led by Dr. Milan Babic. He called traitors those who divide the Serbian people, agents of foreign intelligence services like Ante Markovic are the only ones who believed there are greater problems today and more important things than defending and protecting you. They are selling you to Tudjman. You will not be sold. Instead of calming the crowd, Seselj delivered the following message to the people: We send a message to the Ustasha regime in Croatia: There have been enough Serbian heads that rolled from Ustasha hands. We will avenge Serbian blood."

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Before I ask you to comment, Mr. Stoparic, could we play it again but without the -- the translation. Just for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you recognise the person speaking at 23 seconds?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And the person standing next to him, do you recognise that person?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Stoparic, these two clips that we've heard these two speeches, how does this compare to the type of propaganda you describe in your statement?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Well, you have to know that I described it as propaganda after the war. At that time, it was not propaganda to me. At that time, I saw it as a patriotic speech. Seselj delivered many similar speeches. Depending on the year in which he spoke, they varied a little, but -- I don't know what you want me to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Just answering the question the -- in the manner that you find fit is good enough. Could you tell the Trial Chamber whether Seselj was the only one making such speeches?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: No. At that time, there was a number of politicians speaking about the threat of the Serbian people, such as Vuk Draskovic. But Seselj was the one who most influenced my decision to join in the war effort. I thought at the time that he was telling the whole truth, that everything he was saying was true, and, at that time, I didn't even know Serbian history so well. That's what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, in your statement, you describe the -- what's referred to -- I'd like to find the exact wording. You describe that in -- in May 1991, after the events in Borovo Selo an office opened in the local community centre in Sid. Now, before I ask you follow-up questions to that, I'd like to take a look at tab 94, which is 65 ter number 4770.1, and this is a different part. Now we'll look at clip 20 minute, 27 seconds, to 20 minute, 47 seconds. And again, it's also from the BBC documentary, "The Death of Yugoslavia."

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: "... for protection.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, based on what you know about the events, is Mr. Seselj referring to the same Borovo Selo events that you describe in your statement?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: There was only that one incident in Borovo Selo on the 2nd of May, I believe. After that, the war started. But that's the event that he was referring to, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: In paragraph 6, you describe going to the office of the TO, and you also describe it in paragraph 4, and this office is the recruitment office for the TO SBWS in Sid. Could you describe to the Trial Chamber what, if anything, you heard on the radio about this office before you went in?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: That office was in a building in the centre of Sid. That building housed socio-political organisations, including political parties, Radio Sid, et cetera. The Territorial Defence of the Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem had their offices there. That was written on the door and that's where people gathered who had fled Croatia. Yes, there was a Radio Sid, but I understood Radio Sid to say that people who are from Croatia should report at those premises. I didn't understand that people from Serbia could report and apply too.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And who was making the statements about people from Croatia reporting to the premises of the TO SBWS?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Well, there were many activists there, beginning with Seselj's Chetnik movement which later became the Radical Party. I was told by Veljko Petric, and later I saw it for myself and heard it from various people. On the radio, it was announced by the news caster as some sort of press release or statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you know who -- whose press release or statement it was? Or what party that release or statement came from.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: Considering that Seselj's members of the Radical Party were in that building too, it was from somebody from the Chetnik movement or the Radical Party or perhaps the TO of SBWS. But I think it was Seselj's radicals.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Where geographically was the recruitment office for the TO of SBWS in Sid, Serbia?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: In my town, in Sid, it did not say recruitment office. It was written on the door "TO SBWS," but it was said that that's where people should report and that's where I reported to join. It was in the centre of Sid.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What party, if any, was on the first floor of that building?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC
utterances.text: The Socialist Party, the Serbian Radical Party, Radio Sid was on the top floor. And there were probably more political parties with offices there, but I can't remember the others. Some shared offices. When the SBWS people left, then the Serbian Radical Party and the Socialist Party had the entire floor to themselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Perhaps this would be a good time to tender some of the exhibits that I showed to the witness, Your Honours. At this time we tender the clip from tab 4, 65 ter number 4770.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1725, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, it would be our intention to combine those two clips. We'd split them up, but just the one exhibit number for the two parts that we played. Just so that the record is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Can we do that, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. You do it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So you'd prefer to have two separate numbers for each part --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Not necessarily. If you combine the two clips.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: It has been combined, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It has been combined.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Does that satisfy you, Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And if it hasn't been, we will certainly do so. It has been combined, from what I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we have to -- is it -- we have given it an exhibit number, right?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you. And then the next one would be tab 97, 65 ter 4990.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1726, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And I am mindful of the time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, this is the end of the hearing today. We will have you back tomorrow morning at 9.00. That means that you're not released as a witness and that you are not allowed to discuss your testimony with anyone, and you are not allowed to talk to any of the parties. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The court usher will escort you out of town -- sorry, out of the courtroom, and we will see you tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: If there is nothing else to be discussed, court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
